Prompt: What are the main things that Cybersecurity Specialists do for their job?
Ground_Truth_Answer: Cybersecurity Specialists work with clients to identify security requirements and assess physical and technical security risks to hardware, software, and data. Their duties include applying encryption protocols to secure data, monitoring system access and credentials, and installing and maintaining security tools such as antivirus and threat detection systems. They also monitor networks for cyberattacks or unauthorized activity and respond to security incidents by implementing appropriate protection measures in accordance with the organization’s incident response plan to protect information, data and systems. Additionally, they document emergency measures policies, procedures and tests.
Context: Confer with clients to identify and document requirements, assess physical and technical security risks to data, software and hardware.
Apply encryption protocols and manage keys to ensure security of data is maintained while at rest and in transit.
Monitor access and credentials for information and systems.
Install, test and operate security software and tools such as anti-virus and automated threat detection/prevent systems to ensure security measures are in place and working as intended.
Monitor for cyber attacks, intrusions and unusual, unauthorised or illegal activity.
Plan and carry out security measures in response to cybersecurity events and incidents in accordance with an organization’s incident response plan to protect information, data and systems
Document computer security and emergency measures policies, procedures, and tests.

Prompt: What is the main difference between Web Designers and Web Developers?
Ground_Truth_Answer: The main difference between web designers and web developers is their focus in creating a website. Web designers are responsible for the visual layout, appearance, and user experience, ensuring the website is attractive and easy to navigate. Web developers focus on the technical side by using programming languages to build, modify, and maintain the website’s functionality. While designers plan how the site looks, developers make sure it works properly.
Context: Web designers develop and create the visual presentation, layout and functionality of websites and related applications. They are responsible for ensuring that the website is easy to use, and that the information is easy to access. Web designers are employed in computer software development firms, information technology consulting firms, information technology units throughout the public and private sectors, advertising agencies or they may be self-employed.

Web developers and programmers use a variety of programming languages to design, create and modify websites. They analyse users’ needs to implement content, graphics, performance, and website capacity. They may also integrate websites with other computer applications. They are employed in computer software development firms, information technology consulting firms, information technology units throughout the public and private sectors, advertising agencies or they may be self-employed.

Prompt: Can you simplify the NOC hierarchy for me?
Ground_Truth_Answer: The NOC hierarchy is a system used to organize jobs from broad categories to very specific occupations. The Broad Category (first digit) groups jobs by the general type of work or industry. The TEER Category (second digit) shows the level of training, education, and experience required for the job. Together, these two digits form the Major Group, which contains several related occupations. The Sub-major Group (3 digits) and Minor Group (4 digits) further narrow down the field of work, while the Unit Group (5 digits) is the most specific level and represents the exact occupation.
Context: The Broad Category (first digit) of the classification represents the occupational categorization which is defined by the type of work performed, the field of study, or the industry of employment. There are 10 Broad categories in NOC 2021 Version 1.0.

The TEER Category (second digit) of the classification represents the necessary training, education, experience and responsibilities of the occupation. There are 6 TEER categories in NOC 2021 Version 1.0.

The Major Group (first and second digits) of the classification is represented by the Broad occupational categorization (first digit) and TEER categorization (second digit) together. A major group also encompasses several sub-major groups and thus represents the two-digit code used by the NOC. There are 45 major groups in NOC 2021 Version 1.0.

The Sub-major Group (3-digit) of the classification represents the aggregation of several minor groups and thus represents the three-digit code used by the NOC. There are 89 sub-major groups in NOC 2021 Version 1.0.

The Minor Group (4-digit) of the classification represents the domain in which an occupation is carried out (occupational domain). It is an aggregation of several unit groups and thus represents the four-digit code used by the NOC. There are 162 minor groups in NOC 2021 Version 1.0.

The Unit Group (5-digit) of the classification is the most detailed level of the classification and represents one or several occupations combined within the NOC. There are 516 units groups in NOC 2021 Version 1.0.

Prompt: What are the various credentials needed for someone to pursue the Secondary School teacher occupation?
Ground_Truth_Answer: To become a secondary school teacher, individuals typically need a bachelor’s degree in education, which is often completed after earning a bachelor’s degree in arts or sciences for academic subjects. Those who teach vocational or technical subjects usually complete a bachelor’s degree in education after gaining specialized training or experience in that field. Teachers must also obtain a provincial teaching certificate, and additional training may be required to specialize in areas such as special education or teaching English or French as a second language. In some cases, membership in a provincial or territorial teachers’ association may be required, and department heads usually need several years of teaching experience.

Teachers of vocational or technical subjects require a bachelor’s degree in education which is usually preceded by specialized training or experience in the subject.
Instructors of trades in Quebec require completion of an apprenticeship training program and industry or trade certification.

Prompt: What do Psychologists do? And what are some of the various types of psychologists?
Ground_Truth_Answer: Psychologists study human behaviour and mental processes by assessing behaviour, diagnosing emotional or cognitive disorders, and providing counselling or therapy to individuals and groups. They may use psychological tests, develop treatment and intervention programs, conduct research, publish studies, and present their findings at conferences or workshops. Psychologists may also provide consultation services to organizations and help clients manage physical illnesses or personal challenges. Some types of psychologists include behavioural, child, cognitive, developmental, educational, industrial, neuropsychologists, social psychologists, and sports psychologists.
Context: Examine and assess behaviour, diagnose behavioural, emotional and cognitive disorders, counsel clients and provide therapy.
Help clients manage physical illness and disorders.
Counsel individuals and groups to achieve more effective personal, social and vocational development and adjustment, and offer mediation services.
Use standard psychological tests for assessment.
Plan intervention programs and conduct program evaluation.
Apply psychological theory and principles regarding behaviour and mental processes such as learning, language development, memory and perception to develop treatment programs.
Formulate hypotheses and experimental designs, review literature, conduct studies and publish research papers, educational texts and articles.
Deliver presentations at conferences, workshops or symposia.
Provide consultation services to government and other organizations.
Conduct applied psychology and/or experimental research.

Sub-specialties include behavioural psychology, child psychology, cognitive psychology, developmental psychology, educational psychology, industrial psychology, neuropsychology, social psychology or sports psychology.

Ground_Truth_Answer: To work as a translator, terminologist, or interpreter, individuals usually need a university degree in translation with a specialization in translation, interpretation, or terminology in two languages, including at least one of Canada’s official languages. Alternatively, they may have a degree in a related field such as languages or linguistics with translation courses and two years of experience, or five years of full-time translation experience in two languages. Certification from the Canadian Translators, Terminologists and Interpreters Council may be required, and membership in a provincial or territorial professional association may also be necessary.
